title: PROPAGANDA AI: AN ANALYSIS OF SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Auditing models using paraphrase-controlled prompts on sensitive political topics (e.g., immigration, government surveillance, feminism) and calculating semantic entropy and cross-model disagreement to flag unusually uniform, stance-like responses.

Measuring within-model response uniformity and cross-model divergence on scientific and health topics with multiple legitimate perspectives, such as vaccination and climate change, using bidirectional entailment clustering.

Probing models with questions exploring stances on atheism (praise, condemnation, indifferent stance) and utilizing semantic clustering to detect rigidly uniform and divergent ideological stances compared to peer models.

Evaluating model responses to aspect-based prompts about specific companies (e.g., Tesla, Amazon, McDonald's) regarding governance, labor practices, and impact by computing suspicion scores based on low semantic entropy and high peer disagreement.

Using sentiment-based prompt templates to detect persistent, concept-conditioned sentiment manipulation toward specific public figures, alongside a controlled data-poisoning (LoRA fine-tuning) experiment to implant and detect targeted negative stances.
